title: Traditional Puff Pastry
description: The full classic method with butter block and multiple turns. Ultimate rise, ethereal flakiness, and deep satisfaction. A project worth the effort — make this when pastry is the centrepiece and you have a Sunday afternoon.

ingredients.notes: divided: 350g for Butter Block, 50g for Base Dough

youWillNeed.note: Essential for keeping edges straight and clean
Optional but helpful for keeping butter block square

method.instruction: **Make the détrempe (base dough):** Mix 500 g plain flour, 5 g salt, and 50 g of softened unsalted butter in a bowl. Gradually add ice-cold water while mixing until a smooth, cohesive dough forms. Do not overwork. Wrap in plastic and chill for 30 minutes.

**Prepare the butter block:** Place the remaining 350 g of cold unsalted butter between two sheets of baking paper. Pound with a rolling pin into a 15cm square (about 2cm thick). Keep chilled but pliable — not so cold it cracks, not so warm it smears.

**Enclose the butter:** On a floured surface, roll the détrempe into a cross shape (a central square with four flaps). Place the butter block in the centre. Fold the flaps over to completely enclose the butter, pinching seams to seal.
**First roll:** Roll the dough into a rectangle approximately 20 × 60cm, keeping edges straight with a bench scraper. Fold into thirds like a letter (this is 1 turn).
**Perform the turns:** Rotate the dough 90°. Roll again into a rectangle and fold into thirds. Repeat for a total of 6 turns.
**Rest between turns:** After every 2 turns, wrap and chill the dough for 30 minutes. This prevents butter from softening too much and relaxes the gluten.
**Final rest:** After the 6th turn, wrap tightly and chill for at least 1 hour before using, or overnight for best results.
**To use:** Roll out to desired thickness. Keep chilled until ready to bake — a hot oven (200–220°C / 400–425°F) is essential for maximum rise.

notes.title: Temperature is Everything
notes.content: If butter softens at any point, stop and chill immediately. Warm butter melts into the dough instead of creating distinct layers. Work in a cool kitchen if possible (under 22°C / 72°F).

notes.title: Mark Your Turns
notes.content: Mark each completed turn with a finger indentation in the dough. One dent = one turn. This prevents losing count during a long session.

notes.title: Use European-Style Butter
notes.content: European-style butter has higher fat content (82–86%) and less water. It's more pliable and less likely to crack during rolling. Worth the extra cost for this recipe.

notes.title: Double Turns (Faster Method)
notes.content: Instead of 6 single turns, you can do 4 double turns (fold both ends to the centre, then fold in half). This achieves similar layering in fewer roll-outs but requires more precise rolling.

notes.title: Storage
notes.content: Wrap tightly in plastic wrap and refrigerate for up to 2 days, or freeze for up to 3 months. Thaw frozen dough overnight in the refrigerator before using. Never thaw at room temperature.
